summary.intent: The user wanted to understand the memory loop architecture, then explore adding an MCP tool interface so Claude could pull memories on demand rather than relying solely on hook-based injection.
summary.outcome: A full MCP server implementation was designed and built: two tools (search_memories, save_memory), a new `entire mcp-server` command, and hook installation changes to write mcpServers config into .claude/settings.json. All 14+ tests pass.

repo: Memory loop has two independent axes: mode (off/manual/auto) controls injection, activation_policy (review/auto) controls whether new memories auto-activate. These are frequently conflated.
Injection happens in maybeInjectMemoryLoop() via UserPromptSubmit hook — it's a one-shot write before Claude sees anything, making interactive memory retrieval impossible without MCP.
manual mode has no compelling use case without MCP: it allows curation but never injects, and auto+review_policy already provides safe staging. MCP gives manual mode a real identity.

Facets are the intermediate representation between raw transcripts and memory candidates — structured signals (repeated instructions, friction points, skill opportunities, etc.) extracted from summaries.
Reconciliation uses Jaccard similarity >= 0.50 for dedup; fingerprintForRecord was unexported and needed exporting for the save_memory handler.
AddManualRecord creates records with StatusActive, not StatusCandidate — the save_memory handler needed to bypass it and build records directly to enforce candidate status.
PreviewSelection is too restrictive for MCP search: it calls passesInjectionGate (StatusActive only) and returns empty on empty queries. Search handler needs its own filter+score path.
t.Parallel() cannot be combined with t.Chdir() in Go tests — subagent correctly omitted t.Parallel().

code.finding: Injection gate: if mode != ModeAuto, maybeInjectMemoryLoop returns nil immediately. manual mode never injects.
AddManualRecord sets Status: StatusActive for manual records, not StatusCandidate. Save_memory handler must build records directly to set candidate status.
InstallHooks already had high maintidx lint score before MCP changes — pre-existing issue, not introduced by this work.

workflow: Subagent-driven development pattern: dispatch implementer subagents per task with rich context, verify tests after each task, commit incrementally. Subagents committed their own work, requiring git log checks to track state.
Self-review step on specs before writing plans caught a real ambiguity: search_memories needed to support status:candidate filter, which SelectRelevant/passesInjectionGate doesn't allow.
Reading existing test files before adding new tests is essential for matching style (writeSettingsFile helper pattern, t.Chdir usage, etc.).
Check which files were already modified by subagents before staging — subagents may have already committed, leaving nothing to stage.

friction: User interrupted the brainstorming skill mid-execution twice, requiring 'continue' prompts to resume.
mcp-go dependency wasn't added to go.mod/go.sum until first import — the initial 'go get' step was effectively a no-op.
fingerprintForRecord was unexported, requiring a rename to export it and updating all call sites across the package.
UninstallHooks required multiple Read passes to find the right insertion point for MCP removal code — the function was long and the grep patterns didn't match cleanly.
Pre-existing lint issues (ireturn, maintidx) in modified files created noise when checking for new lint regressions introduced by this work.
open_items: manual mode simplification (remove it or keep with MCP giving it purpose) was discussed but not resolved — the MCP implementation makes manual viable but the naming question remains open.
The MCP server mode gating returns 'memory loop is disabled' for off mode but the exact UX/error message wasn't finalized in the spec.
TUI keybinding to stage memories (i key on Memories tab) was mentioned in design but not implemented.
Full test suite (unit + integration + canary) was kicked off in background at end of session — results not confirmed in transcript.
The InstallHooks maintidx lint issue is pre-existing but adding ~15 lines may push it over threshold — worth a dedicated refactor.
save_memory dedup check uses FingerprintRecord but the reconciliation behavior (update vs reject) for exact matches was not fully specified.
